title: Opportunistic emitter: model admission, metrics, and rollback playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for onboarding and running "opportunistic emitter" model variants in the serving runtime. The emitter is the component that produces speculative tokens ahead of confirmed tokens (opportunistic decode that may later be accepted or discarded). The doc focuses on safe model admission, observable acceptance criteria, automated rollback triggers, and the KV cache invariants that must hold across speculative handoffs.

Context and motivation:
- We have several models that leverage lookahead/emitter behavior to reduce perceived latency and increase throughput for short-turn workloads.
- Prior experiments revealed subtle KV cache staleness bugs and rare token divergence that only show up at scale.
- This playbook codifies a gated rollout path so we can safely surface the latency benefits without regressing output quality or violating customer SLAs.

Goals:
- Define automated and manual acceptance gates for a new opportunistic emitter variant.
- Specify the minimal metrics, smoke tests, and invariants required before promotion to higher rings.
- Describe deterministic rollback actions and quick mitigation steps for incidents.

Non-goals:
- This doc is not a kernel implementation guide (see kernel routing RFC). It focuses on integration, monitoring and ops for model admission.

Terminology:
- emitter: speculative token generator overlaying the primary decode path.
- accept path: the canonical forward decode path that confirms tokens into the KV cache.
- speculative token: token produced by emitter that may be discarded.
- model variant: a signed model build + kernel/quantization profile.

Acceptance criteria (must all be met for promotion):
1) Correctness:
   - Token-level divergence vs baseline <= 0.05% for top-1 across the canary traffic (see QoE harness).
   - End-to-end semantic regression tests: no regression in the top-10 eval prompts used for rollout.
2) Latency:
   - Median tail (p95) token latency improvement >= 8ms over baseline for targeted workload.
   - No upstream: increased latency introduced by the emitter coordination step must be < 2ms on median.
3) Cost/Throughput:
   - Throughput (tokens/s) delta measured under synthetic load within +-5% of expected.
4) Stability / Errors:
   - Error rate (5xx + decode-falls-back-to-safe) < 0.1% over 48h canary.
   - No observed KV cache inconsistency alerts (see KV invariants below).
5) Observability:
   - Full traces with emitter span and kernel selection attributes present in traces.
   - Sampled QoE recordings for at least 10k sessions with diff tool output attached.

KV cache invariants (must be asserted in runtime and by integration tests):
- Invariant A: Any accepted token sequence must overwrite speculative KV entries for the same session and prefix; speculative entries must be tombstoned upon acceptance.
- Invariant B: Speculative entries must carry version tags that are monotonic; the accept path must validate version <= current to avoid regressions.
- Invariant C: Speculative entries must be garbage-collected within configurable TTL (default 10s) if not accepted; a GC trace must be emitted.
- Invariant D: On handoff between kernels (e.g., quantized -> fp16), KV format downgrade/upgrade must be lossless or trigger an immediate safe-fallback.

Admission flow (high-level):
1) Local validation: PR build runs unit tests + KV invariant checks + quick decode smoke.
2) Integration canary (internal traffic): route 0.5% of internal traffic to emitter variant for 48h. Capture full traces, QoE diffs, and KV invariants.
3) External canary (subset of customers): route 1–5% of external production traffic for 72h with heavy sampling and alerting on regressions.
4) Ramp: progressively increase to 25%, 50% with a weekly checkpoint.
5) Promote to global if all metrics are green and product/solutions sign-off is recorded.

Kernel compatibility matrix (summary, updated per model):
- Kernel A (optimized attention v3): supported -- requires emitter to use kernel prefetch hooks.
- Kernel B (quant-llm-4bit): supported with a conservative preference (no early prefix rewrite).
- Kernel C (fp32 fallback): supported but will run on accept path only (no speculative fastpath).
Notes: always include the exact kernel commit hash in the model bundle metadata.

Rollout gating and rollback triggers (automated):
- AUTO-ROLLBACK triggers immediately (0% routing) if any of:
  * QoE divergence rate > 0.3% in 30m sliding window (QoE divergence = semantic eval failures + hallucination score).
  * Error rate spike: decode failures or KV validation failures > 0.5% in 15m.
  * Latency p95 regression > 30% sustained for 10m.
  * Missing critical spans in traces (>1% of sampled requests).
- SOFT-ROLLBACK (throttle to 0.1%): if non-critical anomalies occur (e.g., increased tail, small cost deltas) while ops investigate.
- Manual rollback: runbook for on-call to follow (see "Incident: rollback steps" below).

Automated rollback actions (what the control plane will do):
1) Immediately set routing weight to 0 for the variant.
2) Invalidate speculative KV entries for in-flight sessions belonging to the variant (emit tombstones).
3) Switch affected sessions to accept path kernel with extra tracing enabled.
4) Create incident stub on PagerDuty and attach last 200 affected traces to the incident.

Incident: rollback steps for on-call (short checklist):
- Confirm trigger condition from dashboards and raw logs.
- Execute cloud-control rollback command: rwctl rollout cancel --variant <id> --force
- Run KV audit: scripts/kv-audit --session-sample=500 --since=1h and attach results.
- Notify Solutions/CS for noisy customers (include list of affected session ids).
- Run postmortem triage: tag PRs/commits and schedule deep-dive within 48h.

Required telemetry and dashboards (minimum):
- metric.emitter.token.accept_rate (per model variant, per region)
- metric.emitter.speculative_reuse_ratio (fraction of speculative tokens accepted)
- metric.kv.validation.failures (per session)
- trace.span:emitter.* (include kernel.commit, model.variant, session.id)
- qoe.diff.rate (daily, 1h, 5m rollups)
- alert:emitter.auto_rollback (hooks into routing control plane)
Quality harness / tests to run pre-admission:
- Deterministic replay of 10k golden prompts with top-k sampling parity check.
- Stochastic harness: 100k prompts sampled with production-like temperature and prompt length distribution; compute divergence histograms.
- KV consistency fuzzing across multi-kernel handoffs (inject simulated kernel failovers).
- Long tail soak: 72h soak under 1.5x normal traffic volume.

Open smoke test commands (dev-friendly):
- python infra/smoke/emitter_smoke.py --model <variant> --count 200 --trace
- rwctl trace dump --filter model.variant=<id> --last 1h > /tmp/emitter-traces.json
- scripts/kv-checker.sh --sessions 200 --assert-invariants

Playbook checklist for PR / release notes (must be present in PR description):
- Model bundle hash and kernel commit
- Expected perf gain and measurement harness description
- Canary plan (time windows, traffic %s, rollback thresholds)
- Contact list for triage and escalation
- QoE sample prompts used in acceptance (attach as CSV)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- How to standardize the speculative token TTL across regions with different latency characteristics? (ops input required)
- Should we bake a delta-CRF that compares emitter output to accept path in real time and reduce routing based on model drift? Tradeoffs: added cost vs detection speed.
- Investigate microsecond-level jitter in kernel prefetch hooks observed on AmpereA100 pods; potential HW scheduling implications.

References and related docs:
- See also: kernel-routing-rfc, kv-cache-lease-proposal, speculative-decode-integration-playbook (older).
- GH PR: redwood/realtime#4217 contains the initial emitter prototype and unit harness.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive — the runtime needs clear gates for any speculative/emitter feature. Expect to iterate thresholds after the first 3 internal canaries.
- If you have suggestions for telemetry names or specific alert thresholds, add comments inline or attach linked artifacts.
